title: Data Engineering Trends: Databricks Adoption and AI Integration
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- Databricks usage remains a primary focus for data architecture and silver layer design.
- General data management and cleaning tasks continue to dominate daily engineering workflows.
- Engineers are actively exploring MCP and AI agents to automate pipeline development.
- The job market is shifting as companies prioritize AI-driven cost-saving measures.

Databricks and general data management are the most prominent rising topics this week. Practitioners are heavily focused on architectural decisions, specifically regarding the role of the silver layer in Databricks, including how to handle conformed lookup tables and complex data decoding like Protobuf. Beyond architecture, there is a persistent focus on the fundamentals of data, with many engineers navigating the challenges of cleaning messy CRM data and designing robust data warehouses.

AI integration is significantly influencing the field, with developers experimenting with MCP (Model Context Protocol) to connect Kafka streams to AI agents and building tools to keep coding agents aligned with implementation plans. While some engineers are leveraging these tools to enhance productivity, there is a growing sentiment that the broader job market is slowing down as companies pivot toward AI-driven solutions to reduce costs.

Career development remains a central theme for junior and transitioning engineers. Professionals are balancing traditional skill-building—such as data modeling, system design, and Python pipeline development—with the need to adapt to an era where AI tools like Claude and Cursor are increasingly central to the development lifecycle.
